prompt: In Illinois, it is illegal to drive with a blood-alcohol concentration (BAC) at or above what level?
explanation: Illinois law makes it illegal to drive with a BAC of .08% or more. You can still be convicted of DUI below .08% if your driving ability is impaired.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 51

prompt: An Illinois driver's BAC tests at 0.06%, but the officer saw them weaving and missing a stop sign. Can they be convicted of DUI?
choices: No, a DUI requires a BAC of 0.08% or more
No, unless the BAC is at least 0.07%
Yes, if their driving ability is impaired, even below 0.08%
Only if they also refused a breath test
explanation: Driving at .08% or more is illegal, but the handbook says you can also be convicted of DUI with a BAC under .08% if your driving ability is impaired.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 51

prompt: A 19-year-old Illinois driver is found to have any trace of alcohol in their system. What is the minimum loss of driving privileges?
choices: A warning only, unless BAC is 0.08% or more
A suspension of at least 3 months
A suspension of at least 30 days
A revocation of at least 5 years
explanation: Under Illinois zero tolerance, a driver under 21 with any trace of alcohol loses driving privileges for at least three months. The 0.08% limit is not the cutoff for drivers under 21.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 55

prompt: What is the minimum penalty in Illinois when a driver under age 21 is convicted of a first DUI?
choices: Revocation of driving privileges for at least 2 years
Revocation for at least 1 year, the same as adults
Court supervision with no loss of license
explanation: A driver under 21 convicted of DUI faces revocation for a minimum of two years for a first conviction, longer than the one-year minimum for adult first offenders.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 55

prompt: Under Illinois' implied consent law, what happens to a first-time DUI arrestee who refuses chemical testing?
choices: Driving privileges are suspended for 6 months
Driving privileges are suspended for 3 months
Nothing, unless they are later convicted
Driving privileges are suspended for 1 year
explanation: Refusing chemical testing brings a one-year statutory summary suspension. A failed test (.08% or more) brings six months, so refusing costs more.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 52

prompt: A first-time Illinois DUI arrestee takes a breath test that shows a BAC of 0.09%. How long is the statutory summary suspension?
explanation: A chemical test showing .08% or more (or the THC limits) results in a six-month suspension of driving privileges for a first offender. Refusing the test would mean one year.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 52

prompt: An Illinois driver with a DUI conviction four years ago is arrested again and refuses chemical testing. How long is the suspension?
explanation: Someone with a DUI conviction, supervision or prior summary suspension within five years is a second offender: refusal brings a three-year suspension and a failed test one year.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 52

prompt: What is the minimum license penalty for a first DUI conviction in Illinois for a driver 21 or older?
choices: A fine only, with no license action
explanation: A first DUI conviction results in a minimum one-year revocation. A second conviction within 20 years results in a minimum five-year revocation.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 53

prompt: Illinois law makes it illegal to drive with a THC concentration of at least how many nanograms per milliliter of whole blood?
explanation: The THC limit is 5 nanograms or more per milliliter of whole blood, or 10 nanograms or more per milliliter of other bodily substance. The 10 ng figure is for other bodily substances, not whole blood.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 51

prompt: An adult in Illinois buys cannabis legally and drives home with it. How must it be carried in the vehicle?
choices: Anywhere in the vehicle, as long as it was bought legally
In a closed paper bag on the back seat
In a sealed, odor-proof, child-resistant container
Only in the trunk of the vehicle
explanation: Cannabis may only be transported in a sealed, odor-proof, and child-resistant container, and no driver or passenger may use cannabis in a motor vehicle.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 51

prompt: Where in a vehicle is it illegal to have an alcohol container that has been opened, under Illinois law?
choices: Only if the driver has been drinking
Nowhere, if all passengers are 21 or older
explanation: It is illegal to have alcohol in the passenger area of a vehicle if the container has been opened, and both the driver and passengers can be ticketed for drinking in a vehicle.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 54

prompt: Which of these situations can make a DUI an Aggravated DUI in Illinois?
choices: Committing DUI while driving without a valid license or insurance
Committing a first DUI with a BAC of 0.09%
Being arrested for DUI on a weekend
Refusing a field sobriety test on a first offense
explanation: Aggravated DUI includes a DUI involving death or injury, a third or later DUI, DUI in a school bus or vehicle for hire, and DUI without a valid license, permit or insurance.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 54

prompt: What is the BAC limit for a CDL holder driving a commercial motor vehicle in Illinois?
explanation: A CDL holder may not operate a commercial vehicle with a BAC of .04% or more. In their personal vehicle, the 0.08% limit applies.
ref: Illinois Commercial Driver's License Study Guide (2025), p. 12

prompt: Which Illinois drivers may legally talk on a phone using a hands-free device while driving?
explanation: Handheld phone use is banned for all drivers. Hands-free devices or Bluetooth are allowed only for drivers 19 and older; younger drivers may not use a phone at all except in an emergency.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 25

prompt: A 17-year-old Illinois driver wants to take a call through the car's Bluetooth system while driving. Is this legal?
choices: Yes, because hands-free use is legal for everyone
No, drivers under 19 may not use a phone at all, even hands-free, except to report an emergency
Yes, if the call lasts less than one minute
Yes, if a parent is in the car
explanation: Any wireless phone use while driving, including a hands-free device, is banned for drivers under 19, except to contact police, a health care provider or emergency services in an emergency.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 21

prompt: An adult Illinois driver holds the phone in one hand with the speaker on while driving. Is this hands-free?
choices: No, holding the phone while using the speaker is a violation
Yes, speakerphone always counts as hands-free
Yes, as long as they don't look at the screen
Yes, but only on roads with speed limits under 45 mph
explanation: The handbook states that using a cellphone while holding it and using the speaker phone is not hands-free and violates Illinois law.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 25

prompt: When may an adult Illinois driver use a handheld phone that is not hands-free?
choices: While stopped at a red light with the car in drive
While driving on an empty rural road
While parked on the shoulder of the road
explanation: The only exceptions are reporting an emergency, being parked on the shoulder, or being stopped because traffic is obstructed with the vehicle in neutral or park.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 25

prompt: Which activity on a phone while driving does Illinois law specifically prohibit, even for adults?
choices: Listening to music through the car speakers
Joining a video conference such as a Zoom call
Talking through a single-sided earpiece if 19 or older
explanation: Watching or streaming live video, using video conferencing apps such as Zoom or Teams, and accessing social media on a phone while driving all violate Illinois law.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 25

prompt: Under Illinois' safety belt law, who must wear a safety belt?
choices: Only the driver and front-seat passengers
All drivers and passengers age 8 and older, in front and back seats
Everyone, except in vehicles with air bags
explanation: Illinois requires all drivers and passengers, front and back seats, age 8 and older to wear safety belts, even if the vehicle has air bags. Younger children must be in a child restraint.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 26

prompt: Under Illinois' Child Passenger Protection Act, children younger than what age must be secured in an appropriate child restraint system?
explanation: All children under age 8 must be properly secured in an appropriate child safety restraint system, which includes booster seats used with a lap/shoulder belt.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 26

prompt: Illinois requires a child to ride in a rear-facing child seat until what age, unless the child is over 40 pounds or 40 inches tall?
explanation: Since Jan. 1, 2019, Illinois requires children to be in a rear-facing child restraint until age 2 unless they weigh more than 40 pounds or are more than 40 inches tall.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 27

prompt: Illinois law prohibits playing a vehicle sound system so loud that it can be heard how far away from the moving vehicle?
explanation: You may not play a sound system at a volume that can be heard 75 feet or more from a vehicle being driven on a highway.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 39

prompt: Unless another limit is posted, what is the speed limit on Illinois interstates and tollways?
explanation: Illinois' default limit on interstates and tollways is 70 mph. Highways with four lanes default to 65 mph, and other highways to 55 mph.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 27

prompt: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit on an Illinois highway with four lanes that is not an interstate?
explanation: The default limit is 65 mph on highways with four lanes, 70 mph on interstates and tollways, and 55 mph on other highways and rural roads.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 27

prompt: Unless otherwise posted, what is the speed limit on Illinois rural roads and two-lane highways?
explanation: Other highways and rural areas have a 55 mph limit unless posted otherwise.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 27

prompt: What is the speed limit in Illinois city and town areas when no other limit is posted?
explanation: The statewide default for city/town areas is 30 mph, although local municipalities may post different limits.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 27

prompt: When does the 20 mph Illinois school zone speed limit apply?
choices: Every day from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.
On school days between 6:30 a.m. and 4 p.m. when children are present and signs are posted
Only when a crossing guard is in the street
Any time school buses are on the road
explanation: School zones have a 20 mph limit on school days between 6:30 a.m. and 4 p.m. when children are present and signs are posted. Phone use (except hands-free) is also banned there.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 27

prompt: There is no posted minimum speed on the Illinois road you are driving. What does the handbook say about driving slowly?
choices: You should not drive so slowly that you interfere with the normal movement of traffic
There is no limit on how slowly you may drive
You must always drive within 5 mph of the posted limit
You must drive at least 40 mph on any highway
explanation: When minimum limits are not posted, you should not drive so slowly as to interfere with the normal movement of traffic. Where a minimum is posted, driving below it is illegal unless needed for safety.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 27

prompt: What following distance rule does the Illinois handbook recommend in good road and weather conditions?
explanation: Illinois recommends the three-second rule on a good road in good weather, with more distance in poor conditions.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 86

prompt: How much following distance does the Illinois handbook say to allow when behind a motorcycle?
choices: Two seconds, the same as for a car
At least three to four seconds
explanation: Allow at least three to four seconds behind a motorcycle so the rider has room to maneuver in an emergency. Motorcycles can stop faster than cars in dry conditions.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 45

prompt: You drive through a posted Illinois construction zone at 9 p.m. on a Sunday, and no workers are present. Must you obey the posted construction zone speed limit?
choices: No, it applies only when workers are present
Yes, it applies 24 hours a day, seven days a week
No, it applies only on weekdays
Only if a flagger is directing traffic
explanation: Motorists must obey the posted construction zone speed limit 24 hours a day, seven days a week, whether or not workers are present.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 28

prompt: In an Illinois business or residential area, how far before turning must you give a continuous turn signal?
explanation: In business or residential areas, signal continuously for at least 100 feet before turning; in other areas, at least 200 feet.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 33

prompt: You are about to turn off an Illinois rural highway. How far before the turn must your signal begin?
explanation: Outside business and residential areas, the turn signal must be given at least 200 feet before turning.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 33

prompt: In Illinois, may you turn right at a steady red light?
choices: Yes, without stopping if no one is coming
Yes, after a complete stop and yielding, unless a sign prohibits it
Only when a green arrow is also lit
explanation: You may turn right at a red light unless a sign prohibits it, but you must first come to a complete stop and yield to traffic and pedestrians.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 80

prompt: When does Illinois allow a left turn on a red light?
choices: From any street onto a one-way street
From a one-way street onto another one-way street with traffic moving to the left, after stopping
From a two-way street onto a one-way street
Never; left turns on red are always illegal
explanation: After a complete stop and yielding, you may turn left on red only from a one-way street onto another one-way street that has traffic moving to the left.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 80

prompt: You are stopped at an Illinois intersection facing a steady red arrow pointing right. No sign prohibits turning on red. What may you do?
choices: Make the right turn after a complete stop and yielding to traffic and pedestrians
Wait until a green arrow appears
Turn right only if a police officer waves you through
explanation: A steady red arrow normally means wait for a green arrow, but Illinois makes an exception: you may turn right on a red arrow after a complete stop, yielding to traffic and pedestrians.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 81

prompt: You come to an Illinois intersection where the traffic signals are completely dark because of a power outage. What must you do?
choices: Drive through carefully if the road looks clear
Slow down and yield only to traffic on your right
Proceed if you are on the larger road
Treat it as an all-way stop: stop completely, then yield before entering
explanation: When traffic signals are not working, you must treat the intersection as an all-way stop by coming to a complete stop, unless law enforcement directs otherwise.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 80

prompt: Another driver is behind you on a two-lane road. Is it legal in Illinois to flash your turn signals to let them know it is safe to pass?
choices: Yes, it is a required courtesy
No, flashing turn signals as a courtesy or do-pass signal is against the law
Yes, if you use the right signal
explanation: Illinois law prohibits flashing turn signals as a courtesy or do-pass signal to other drivers.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 31

prompt: You come upon a funeral procession at an Illinois intersection. What must you do?
choices: Yield only to the lead vehicle
Yield to every vehicle in the procession and not cut between them
Go when your light turns green, even if the procession is still passing
Merge into the procession to get through faster
explanation: Motorists must yield to all vehicles in a funeral procession and should not drive between its vehicles unless directed by police. Joining a procession to gain the right of way is prohibited.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 29

prompt: An ambulance with its siren and flashing lights comes up behind you on an Illinois street. What must you do?
choices: Immediately pull to the right side of the road and let it pass, stopping if needed
Speed up to stay ahead of it
Pull to the left side of the road
explanation: Illinois law requires motorists to immediately pull to the right side of the road and let the emergency vehicle pass. A complete stop may be necessary.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 28

prompt: On a four-lane Illinois highway, you approach a police car stopped on the shoulder with its lights flashing. What does Illinois law require?
choices: Keep your speed and lane, since it is on the shoulder
Stop completely behind the police car
Honk to warn the officer and continue
Yield, change to a lane away from it if possible, otherwise slow down and proceed with caution
explanation: For a stationary emergency or maintenance vehicle with flashing lights, you must yield, move to a lane away from it when possible, and otherwise reduce speed and proceed with caution.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 28

prompt: On a four-lane Illinois highway, you approach a disabled car on the shoulder with its hazard lights on. What does Illinois law require?
choices: Nothing; the rule applies only to police cars
Stop behind it and offer help
Change lanes away from it if safe; otherwise reduce speed while passing
Pass it as quickly as possible
explanation: Illinois law requires drivers approaching a disabled vehicle using hazard lights on a four-lane highway to change lanes away from it if safe, or else slow down until well past it.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 48

prompt: Illinois law prohibits photography and phone use within how many feet of an emergency scene, with limited exceptions?
explanation: Illinois law prohibits photography and wireless phone use within 500 feet of an emergency scene, except in certain circumstances.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 28

prompt: A pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk ahead of you in Illinois. What must you do?
choices: Come to a complete stop and yield
Slow down and steer around the pedestrian
Stop only if the pedestrian is in your lane
explanation: Illinois requires a driver to come to a complete stop and yield when a pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 30

prompt: When passing a person walking on the shoulder of an Illinois road, how much space must you leave?
explanation: When passing a pedestrian walking on the road or shoulder, keep a minimum of 3 feet between your vehicle and the pedestrian.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 31

prompt: You are on a two-lane Illinois road and a school bus coming toward you stops with its red lights flashing and stop arm out. What must you do?
choices: Slow down and pass carefully, since it is on the other side
Stop, then go once the children are on the bus
Stop and stay stopped until the arm is withdrawn and the lights turn off, or the driver signals you on
Continue, because only traffic behind the bus must stop
explanation: Unless you are on a four-lane roadway, you must stop for a school bus loading or unloading from either direction and stay stopped until the stop arm is withdrawn and lights are off, or the bus driver signals you to pass.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 36

prompt: In which situation does Illinois NOT require you to stop for a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended?
choices: You are on a two-lane road and the bus is coming toward you
You are on a four-lane roadway and the bus is stopped in the opposite direction
You are behind the bus on a four-lane roadway
The bus is stopped in a school parking lot
explanation: You need not stop only when both vehicles are on a four-lane roadway and the bus is stopped in the opposite direction. You must stop on two-lane roads, private roads and school parking lots.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 35

prompt: What is the penalty in Illinois for a conviction for passing a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended?
choices: License suspension, a mandatory $300 fine and community service
explanation: A conviction for passing a stopped school bus results in suspension of your license, a mandatory $300 fine and community service set by the court.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 36

prompt: When passing on an Illinois two-lane highway, you must return to your lane before coming within how many feet of an oncoming vehicle?
explanation: You must return to your lane before getting within 200 feet of an oncoming vehicle, and should not cut back in until the whole vehicle you passed is visible in your rearview mirror.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 31

prompt: On an Illinois two-lane, two-way road, passing is NOT allowed within how many feet of an intersection or railroad crossing?
explanation: Passing on a two-lane, two-way roadway is not allowed within 100 feet of an intersection or railroad crossing, or when your view is blocked within 100 feet of a bridge, viaduct or tunnel.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 32

prompt: A two-lane road through an Illinois construction zone has a broken center line and no NO PASSING signs. May you pass a slow vehicle there?
choices: Yes, because the center line is broken
No, all construction zones in Illinois are no-passing zones
Yes, if no workers are present
Yes, if you stay under the speed limit
explanation: The handbook states that all construction zones in Illinois are no-passing zones.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 32

prompt: On an Illinois interstate, when may you drive in the left lane?
choices: Mainly when passing; other exceptions include no one behind you, heavy traffic, bad weather or an obstruction
Any time you are going the speed limit
Only when exiting on the left
Never; the left lane is for emergency vehicles
explanation: On interstates and full access-controlled freeways, you may not drive in the left lane except to pass, unless an exception applies, such as no vehicle directly behind you, congestion, weather, an obstruction, or yielding to emergency or construction vehicles.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 32

prompt: Two lanes merge into one on an Illinois highway during heavy, slow traffic. What does the handbook advise?
choices: Move into the open lane as soon as you see the sign
Stay in the ending lane and force your way in
Stop and wait for a gap in the open lane
Use both lanes up to the merge point, then take turns merging (the zipper merge)
explanation: During congestion, use both lanes up to the lane reduction point and merge there, alternating turns: the zipper merge. When traffic is light, merge early.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 74

prompt: What is the Dutch Reach that Illinois recommends when you get out of a parked car?
choices: Opening the door quickly to limit the time it is open
Looking only in the side mirror before opening the door
Opening the driver's door with your right hand so you turn and look back for bicyclists and traffic
Opening the passenger door instead of the driver's door
explanation: Using your right hand to open the driver's door turns your upper body so you can check for oncoming vehicles and bicyclists. You may not open a door on the traffic side unless it is safe.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 33

prompt: In Illinois, you may not park within how many feet of a fire hydrant?
explanation: Standing or parking a vehicle within 15 feet of a fire hydrant is prohibited.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 38

prompt: How close may you park to a crosswalk at an intersection in Illinois?
explanation: Standing or parking is prohibited within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 39

prompt: In Illinois, you may not park within how many feet of a STOP sign, YIELD sign, or traffic signal?
explanation: Standing or parking is prohibited within 30 feet of a STOP sign, YIELD sign or traffic control signal.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 39

prompt: In Illinois, parking is prohibited within how many feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing?
explanation: Parking is prohibited within 50 feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 39

prompt: In Illinois, you may not stand or park within how many feet of a fire station driveway?
explanation: Standing or parking is prohibited within 20 feet of a fire station driveway.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 39

prompt: When parallel parking on an Illinois street with two-way traffic, how close to the curb must your right-hand wheels be?
explanation: Park with your right-hand wheels parallel to and within 12 inches of the curb. On a one-way street, park within 12 inches of the right or left curb.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 38

prompt: Can a car with a disability placard park on the striped area next to an accessible parking space in Illinois?
choices: Yes, if it displays a placard
Yes, if the accessible space is full
No, the striped area is part of the reserved space and no vehicle may park there
explanation: The striped area next to an accessible space is part of the reserved space, and vehicles may not park there even with a placard or disability plates.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 38

prompt: Under Illinois law, may you briefly stop in a marked bike lane to drop off a passenger if no bicyclists are around?
choices: Yes, if you stay under one minute
Yes, with your hazard lights on
No, vehicles may not park, idle, or pick up or drop off passengers in bike lanes
Yes, if no cyclists are in sight
explanation: Vehicles are not allowed to drive, park, idle, or drop off or pick up passengers in bike lanes, even when no bicyclists are present.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 45

prompt: When a railroad crossing signal is flashing or the gate is down, how far from the crossing must you stop in Illinois?
explanation: You must stop within 15-50 feet of a railroad crossing if there is a stop sign, the signal is flashing, the gate is lowered, a flagger signals, or a train is approaching.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 36

prompt: Your car stalls on railroad tracks in Illinois. After everyone gets out and calls 911, which way should you move away from the tracks?
choices: At a 45-degree angle, toward the direction the train is coming from
Straight down the tracks away from the train
At a 45-degree angle, away from the direction of the train
Stay next to the car to guide the train crew
explanation: Move away from the tracks at a 45-degree angle in the direction of the train. This keeps you clear of debris thrown forward if the train hits the car.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 36

prompt: When passing a bicyclist in Illinois, how much space must you leave?
choices: At least 3 feet, measured from your side mirror
explanation: Pass bicyclists slowly, leaving at least 3 feet from the edge of your side mirror; if there is not 3 feet of space, wait to pass. This includes cyclists on the shoulder or in a bike lane.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 46

prompt: When may bicyclists in Illinois ride more than two abreast?
choices: On any road with a speed limit under 30 mph
Only on paths or parts of roadways set aside for bicycles only
explanation: Bicyclists may ride two abreast if they do not impede normal traffic. Riding more than two abreast is prohibited except on paths or roadway areas set aside for exclusive bicycle use.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 46

prompt: In Illinois, a motorcyclist is stopped at a red light that does not turn green. After how long may the rider proceed, after yielding?
explanation: If a red light fails to turn green after 120 seconds, a motorcyclist may proceed through the intersection after yielding the right of way to oncoming traffic.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 44

prompt: It starts raining lightly and you turn on your windshield wipers during the day in Illinois. What else does Illinois law require?
choices: Slowing to 10 mph under the limit
explanation: Illinois law requires you to use your headlights whenever you are operating your windshield wipers.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 88

prompt: Besides sunset to sunrise and when wipers are needed, when should headlights be used in Illinois?
choices: When objects 200 feet away cannot be seen
When objects 1,000 feet away cannot be seen
explanation: Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and whenever conditions require wipers, and should also be used when objects 1,000 feet away cannot be seen.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 95

prompt: In Illinois, you must dim your high beams when an oncoming vehicle is within how many feet?
explanation: Bright lights must be dimmed 500 feet before meeting an oncoming vehicle, and 300 feet before passing a vehicle ahead.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 95

prompt: You are using high beams at night and come up behind another vehicle going the same way. When must you dim them in Illinois?
choices: Only when you start to pass
explanation: Illinois requires bright lights to be dimmed 300 feet before passing a vehicle, so dim them when within 300 feet of a vehicle ahead. The 500-foot rule is for oncoming vehicles.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 95

prompt: When must an Illinois driver file a crash report, regardless of fault?
choices: When the crash involves death, injury, or property damage over $1,500
Only when the driver is at fault
Only when property damage is over $5,000
Only when police come to the scene
explanation: Regardless of fault, the driver must file a crash report when the crash involves death, bodily injury or property damage of more than $1,500 ($500 if any vehicle is uninsured).
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 57

prompt: If any vehicle in an Illinois crash is uninsured, a crash report is required when property damage is more than what amount?
explanation: Normally the threshold is more than $1,500, but if any vehicle involved is uninsured, a report must be filed for damage over $500.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 57

prompt: According to the Illinois handbook, how long does a driver have to report a crash after it occurs?
explanation: The handbook states that a driver has 30 minutes to report a crash after it occurs, and drivers should notify police immediately.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 58

prompt: You crash on a rural Illinois road and no officer comes to the scene. Whom should you notify?
choices: The county sheriff or the Illinois State Police
The Secretary of State, within 30 days
No one, if nobody is hurt
explanation: If no officer is at the scene, report at the nearest police station as soon as possible. In rural areas, notify the county sheriff or Illinois State Police. If the driver can't report, a passenger must.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 58

prompt: In Illinois, what happens to a driver convicted of leaving the scene of a crash in which someone was injured?
choices: The Secretary of State must revoke their license
They must take a defensive driving class
explanation: When a death or personal injury occurred, the Secretary of State is required to revoke the license of a driver convicted of leaving the scene.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 58

prompt: Your car breaks down on a busy multi-lane Illinois highway. What do Illinois' stranded motorist protocols say to do after pulling onto the right shoulder?
choices: Get out and walk to the nearest exit
Stand behind the car to wave traffic around it
Raise the hood and try to fix the problem
Stay in the car with your seatbelt on, turn on hazard lights and call 911
explanation: On high-capacity roads, pull as far right as possible, remain in your vehicle with your seatbelt on, turn on hazard lights, call 911 and wait for responders.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 93

prompt: If your vehicle breaks down on the Illinois Tollway, what number may you call besides 911?
explanation: On the Illinois Tollway, stay in your vehicle with your seatbelt on and hazard lights flashing, and call *999 or 911.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 93

prompt: You are pulled over by Illinois police. What should you do while the officer approaches?
choices: Get out and walk toward the squad car
Stay in the vehicle with both hands on the steering wheel
Reach under the seat for your insurance card
Get out and open the trunk
explanation: Stay in the vehicle with both hands visible on the wheel until the officer tells you otherwise. Getting out can be seen as aggressive, and tell the officer before reaching for documents.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 24

prompt: What is the youngest age at which you can get an Illinois instruction permit?
choices: 15, when enrolled in an approved driver education course
15 and 6 months, with no driver education
explanation: At 15-17 you can get an instruction permit with proof that you are enrolled in, or will start within 30 days, an approved driver education course.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 19

prompt: How long must an Illinois driver under 18 hold an instruction permit before getting a license?
explanation: Permit holders age 15-17 must hold the permit for at least nine consecutive months, with no driving infractions during that period.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 19

prompt: How much supervised practice driving must an Illinois driver under 18 complete before getting a license?
explanation: Illinois requires at least 50 hours of supervised behind-the-wheel driving, including 10 hours at night, in addition to driver education.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 19

prompt: Who may supervise an Illinois permit holder outside of driver education?
choices: Any licensed driver age 18 or older, in any seat
A parent, guardian or adult age 21+ with a valid license and at least 1 year of driving experience, in the front seat
Any adult age 25 or older, even without a license
explanation: The supervisor must be a parent, legal guardian or responsible adult age 21 or older with a valid license and at least one year of driving experience, sitting in the front passenger seat.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 19

prompt: What are the nighttime driving restrictions for Illinois drivers under 18 on Sunday through Thursday nights?
choices: No driving from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m.
No driving from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m.
No driving from midnight to 5 a.m.
No driving from 9 p.m. to 5 a.m.
explanation: Permit holders and Initial Licensing Phase drivers may not drive Sunday-Thursday from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m., or Friday-Saturday from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. Local curfews may differ.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 21

prompt: A 16-year-old Illinois driver wants to drive home from a party at 10:30 p.m. on a Saturday. Is this allowed under the GDL nighttime restriction?
choices: No, the restriction starts at 10 p.m. every night
No, the restriction starts at 9 p.m. on weekends
Yes, weekend nights have no restriction
Yes, the Friday-Saturday restriction starts at 11 p.m.
explanation: On Friday and Saturday nights, the GDL restriction runs from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m., so 10:30 p.m. is allowed (unless a local curfew differs). Sunday-Thursday it starts at 10 p.m.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 21

prompt: During the first 12 months of licensing (or until 18), how many passengers under age 20 may an Illinois teen driver carry, not counting family members?
explanation: For the first 12 months or until 18, whichever comes first, passengers are limited to one person under 20, unless the passengers are the driver's siblings, stepsiblings, children or stepchildren.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 21

prompt: A 16-year-old has held an Illinois license for three months. Which group of passengers may she legally drive?
choices: Two friends from school, both age 17
explanation: In the first 12 months, she may carry only one passenger under 20 unless the passengers are siblings, stepsiblings, children or stepchildren. Her two brothers qualify; two unrelated teens under 20 do not.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 21

prompt: Can an Illinois parent who consented to a 16-year-old's license later cancel it?
choices: Yes, at any time and for any reason until the driver turns 18
No, once issued the license can't be canceled
Only if the teen gets a ticket
explanation: The parent or guardian who gave consent may cancel the minor's license at any time, for any reason, until the driver turns 18.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 22

prompt: An Illinois driver under 21 is convicted of two moving violations within 24 months. What is the minimum consequence?
choices: A license suspension of at least 30 days
explanation: A driver under 21 convicted of two or more moving violations within 24 months faces a minimum 30-day suspension. For adults, suspension may follow three traffic violation convictions in 12 months.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 23

prompt: An Illinois driver age 30 may have their license suspended after how many traffic violation convictions within 12 months?
explanation: Three traffic violation convictions during a 12-month period can lead to suspension. For drivers under 21, it is two violations within 24 months.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 63

prompt: A 19-year-old who has never been licensed and never took driver education wants an Illinois license. What must they complete first?
choices: A 30-hour high school driver education course
A six-hour Adult Driver Education Course from a certified provider
Nothing; driver education rules end at 18
explanation: First-time applicants age 18-20 who never completed an approved driver ed program must take a six-hour Adult Driver Education Course from a Secretary of State-certified provider.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 8

prompt: What are Illinois' minimum liability insurance limits?
choices: $25,000 per person / $50,000 per crash for injury, $20,000 property damage
explanation: Illinois requires at least $25,000 for injury or death of one person, $50,000 for more than one person, and $20,000 for damage to another's property.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 101

prompt: What happens to an Illinois driver convicted of driving without the mandatory insurance?
choices: They lose driving privileges for 1 year, with a permit available
Their vehicle is sold at auction
They lose driving privileges for at least 3 months and pay a $100 reinstatement fee
explanation: Drivers convicted of mandatory insurance violations lose their driving privileges for at least three months and must pay a $100 reinstatement fee, with no driving permit available.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 58

prompt: Illinois' vision standard for a driver's license requires a minimum visual acuity of what, with or without corrective lenses?
explanation: The minimum is 20/40 with or without corrective lenses. Drivers whose acuity is between 20/41 and 20/70 are limited to daylight driving only.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 16

prompt: How many attempts do you get to pass each Illinois driver's license exam?
choices: Three attempts within one year of paying the application fee
One attempt; then you must wait 30 days
explanation: You are allowed three attempts to pass each exam within one year from the date you paid your application fee.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 16

prompt: What is the minimum age to get an Illinois driver's license?
explanation: You must be at least 16 to get an Illinois driver's license. At 15 you can only get an instruction permit, and drivers under 18 must finish driver education and 50 practice hours first.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 7

prompt: An Illinois driver turns 18 and enters the Full Licensing Phase. Which GDL rule still applies to them?
choices: No phone use at all while driving, even hands-free, until age 19
The 10 p.m. weekday nighttime driving restriction
Supervision by an adult age 21 or older
explanation: In the Full Licensing Phase (ages 18-20) no age-related restrictions apply, except that any phone use while driving, including hands-free, is banned for drivers under 19 except in an emergency.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 22

prompt: A 35-year-old Illinois driver wants to send a quick text while driving on an open road. Is this legal?
choices: No, texting while driving is illegal for all drivers
Yes, if the phone is mounted on the dashboard
Yes, if the vehicle is going under 30 mph
explanation: Illinois law prohibits texting, using handheld cellphones and other electronic communications while driving, at any age. Being 19 or older only allows hands-free calling.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 25

prompt: According to the Illinois handbook, when may you drive at the maximum posted speed limit?
choices: At any time, as long as you do not exceed it
explanation: You may drive at the maximum allowable speed only under safe conditions. You must slow down when approaching intersections, curves, hill tops and narrow or winding roads.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 27

prompt: Under Illinois law, where is stopping, standing, or parking prohibited even if no sign is posted?
choices: On a residential street at night
explanation: Statewide rules prohibit stopping, standing or parking on a sidewalk, on a crosswalk, or within an intersection, as well as double parking and parking on bridges or railroad tracks.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 38

prompt: Unless another limit is posted, what is the speed limit in an Illinois alley?
explanation: The default limit in alleys is 15 mph, compared with 30 mph in city/town areas and 20 mph in school zones when children are present.
ref: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, p. 27

prompt: Does Illinois law require motorcycle riders to wear a helmet?
choices: No, but the manual strongly recommends a properly fitted helmet
Yes, all riders must wear one
explanation: A helmet is not required under Illinois law, but a properly fitted helmet greatly reduces the chance of a fatal head injury. Face or eye protection and protective clothing are also recommended.
ref: Illinois Motorcycle Operator Manual (2025), p. 6

prompt: In Illinois, may a motorcyclist ride between two lanes of cars moving in the same direction (lane splitting)?
choices: Yes, if traffic is moving under 30 mph
Yes, if the rider uses the horn
No, riding between two vehicles going the same direction is prohibited unless an unobstructed lane is available
explanation: Illinois prohibits riders from passing between two vehicles going the same direction unless an unobstructed traffic lane is available to pass safely.
ref: Illinois Motorcycle Operator Manual (2025), p. 5

prompt: When may an Illinois motorcyclist pass another vehicle on the right?
choices: Only when there is at least 8 feet of unobstructed pavement to the right of the vehicle
explanation: Riders may not pass on the right unless there is unobstructed pavement at least 8 feet wide to the right of the vehicle being passed.
ref: Illinois Motorcycle Operator Manual (2025), p. 5

prompt: An Illinois motorcyclist waits at a red light that doesn't turn green. What does Illinois law allow?
choices: Proceeding after the light fails to change for at least 120 seconds, after yielding
Running the light at once if no cars are around
Turning around and leaving by the sidewalk
explanation: Motorcycles may proceed through a red light that fails to turn green within a reasonable time of not less than 120 seconds, after yielding to oncoming traffic.
ref: Illinois Motorcycle Operator Manual (2025), p. 5

prompt: What does an Illinois Class L license allow you to operate?
choices: Motor-driven cycles with less than 150cc displacement
explanation: Class L covers motor-driven cycles under 150cc. Class M covers any motorcycle or motor-driven cycle.
ref: Illinois Motorcycle Operator Manual (2025), p. 4

prompt: What must a 16- or 17-year-old complete to get a motorcycle classification on an Illinois license?
choices: Nothing beyond a Class D license
A motorcycle training course approved by IDOT
explanation: Riders age 16 or 17 must complete a motorcycle training course approved by the Illinois Department of Transportation (IDOT) to get a motorcycle classification. A written test alone is not enough at that age.
ref: Illinois Motorcycle Operator Manual (2025), p. 4

prompt: What are the limits on an Illinois motorcycle instruction permit?
choices: Any time, with any licensed passenger
Daylight riding only, supervised by a licensed rider age 21+ with at least 1 year of experience
explanation: The permit allows riding only during daylight hours, under the direct supervision of a licensed motorcycle operator age 21 or older with at least one year of experience.
ref: Illinois Motorcycle Operator Manual (2025), p. 4

prompt: A rider 16 or older completes an IDOT Motorcycle Rider Education Course. What does this mean for Illinois licensing?
choices: They still must take both exams at a DMV
They need not pass a written or driving exam at a DMV; the completion card is valid for one year
They get a Class M license that never expires
They may skip the vision screening only
explanation: Riders 16 and older who complete an IDOT Motorcycle Rider Education Course are not required to pass a written or driving exam at a DMV. The course completion card is valid for one year.
ref: Illinois Motorcycle Operator Manual (2025), p. 4

prompt: When does Illinois law require a motorcycle's headlight to be on?
choices: Whenever the motorcycle is operated on streets and highways
explanation: Illinois law requires the motorcycle headlight to be on when operating on streets and highways, day or night.
ref: Illinois Motorcycle Operator Manual (2025), p. 21

prompt: What is an Illinois rider guilty of for operating a motorcycle on one wheel?
choices: No offense, if done on a straight road
Reckless driving, or aggravated operating of a motorcycle on one wheel
explanation: A person who operates a motorcycle on one wheel is guilty of reckless driving or aggravated operating of a motorcycle on one wheel.
ref: Illinois Motorcycle Operator Manual (2025), p. 5
